title: H100 tuned preset: scheduler defaults + kernel-selection toggles + perf targets
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Build and validate the H100 tuning preset for the hardware tuning profiles pack. Scope includes:
- Scheduler parameter defaults (continuous batching behavior, prefill/decode fairness, backpressure/queue limits, streaming stability knobs)
- Kernel selection toggles + heuristics (H100-specific auto-select by sequence-length buckets; safe-by-default)
- Perf targets + validation criteria (p50/p95 latency bounds, throughput tokens/sec, retry rate, stability)

This ticket is the "H100 preset" deliverable; schema/loader/override-order are owned in ENG-4822/ENG-4823.

Primary goals:
1) Improve throughput/unit cost for typical hosted + dedicated H100 pools without violating tail latency SLOs.
2) Make behavior predictable and rollbackable via profile pack + canary gates.
3) Document expected behavior envelope (workload assumptions + known trade-offs).

Non-goals:
- New kernels from scratch
- Customer-specific bespoke tuning (handled via Support/Solutions follow-ups)

acceptance_criteria:
Functional:
- H100 profile exists in the pack with two modes:
  - balanced (default): safe tail-latency posture
  - throughput-first (opt-in): higher batching/aggression with explicit caveats
- Profile is selectable by GPU detection (H100 SXM + PCIe variants) and can be overridden per pool/deployment.
- Runtime logs/metrics expose selected profile + mode + override source (for oncall triage).

Performance (measured on workload matrix for at least 3 model families):
- Balanced mode:
  - Throughput: +8–15% tokens/sec at steady-state concurrency vs baseline runtime defaults
  - Latency: p95 <= +5% vs baseline for streaming workloads; p95 <= +8% for non-streaming
  - Stability: retry rate and timeouts not worse than baseline; no increase in OOMs
- Throughput-first mode:
  - Throughput: +15–25% tokens/sec vs baseline on "throughput" matrix rows
  - Latency: may regress; must be explicitly documented and gated behind opt-in mode

Operational:
- Perf-canary gates updated to cover key H100 rows and catch tail-latency regressions.
- Rollback is one toggle (disable profile pack or pin to baseline profile) and documented in runbook.

Documentation:
- "Expected behavior" section drafted for H100 describing when balanced vs throughput-first should be used and what workload assumptions apply (seq-len mix, concurrency, streaming vs non-streaming).
implementation_plan:
1) Align on baseline and workload envelope
- Use the workload matrix runner as the canonical benchmark harness; pin prompt sets + seq-len buckets.
- Define acceptance rows as the gating set for H100 balanced default (streaming-focused + mixed seq-len).

2) Scheduler preset (balanced + throughput-first)
- Balanced default emphasis:
  - Keep prefill/decode fairness enabled; avoid starvation under mixed workloads.
  - Conservative queue depth / backpressure to prevent p95 blowups when request burst arrives.
  - Streaming stability: avoid large micro-batches on decode when stream cadence matters.
- Throughput-first emphasis:
  - Increase max batch tokens and queue depth; allow more aggressive continuous batching.
  - Still enforce hard guardrails (max in-flight tokens; safety cutoff on queue age).

3) Kernel auto-selection heuristics (H100)
- Enable H100-specific kernel toggles keyed off sequence-length buckets.
- Explicitly document which kernels are allowed and when the runtime may fall back.
- Guardrails: if detection is ambiguous or kernel mismatch errors occur, fall back to baseline safe set.

4) Validate and iterate
- Run matrix on H100 SXM and PCIe pool variants.
- Compare p50/p95, tokens/sec, GPU mem usage, and error/retry metrics.
- Triage regressions with Kernels/Scheduling; add targeted regression tests if needed.

5) Ship behind profile pack version
- Default H100 pools to balanced mode after canary passes.
- Keep throughput-first opt-in for Dedicated/Private advanced users (documented and supportable).
notes_and_tradeoffs:
Key trade-offs surfaced so far:
- Scheduler fairness vs throughput: aggressive batching can increase tokens/sec but harms p95 for interactive/streaming traffic. Balanced mode should bias to stable p95.
- Mixed seq-len: tuning for long-context prefill can starve short requests if fairness is too weak; we need explicit fairness knobs + backpressure.
- Fleet variance: H100 SXM vs PCIe and different clock/HBM behavior can shift optimal settings; profile must keep safe defaults and avoid brittle micro-optimizations.

Decision: default the H100 preset to balanced mode (safe-by-default). Throughput-first exists but is opt-in and must clearly state tail-latency risk.
risk_register:
Risks:
- Tail latency regression due to prefill/decode scheduling changes (observed once during early validation).
- Perf-canary flakiness/noise causing false positives; ensure gates are robust before ramping rollout.
- Kernel selection mismatch under unusual seq-len distributions or model variants; must include safe fallback and high-signal logging.

Mitigations:
- Gate on p95 + error/retry rates; require canary stability window.
- Add runtime metrics for effective preset + key knobs.
- Ensure rollback path is documented and tested (disable profile per pool).
